does: Fries tomato or red pepper paste in hot fat until it darkens and begins to catch on the pan. This softens the raw edge before the liquid goes in.

intro.what: Tomato paste is fried in fat until it darkens and begins to stick.
intro.why: Frying the paste turns a sharp, tinny taste into a deep sweet one, and what sticks to the pan can be lifted with a splash of liquid.

how: Have the fat hot and any onion already soft.
Add the paste and spread it over the bottom of the pan, stirring all the time.
Cook until it turns a deep brick red and starts to stick, then add the liquid straight away.

cues.text: The paste turns from bright red to a deep brick red and leaves a coat on the pan.
The sharp smell turns sweet and toasty.

mistakes.mistake: Adding the liquid as soon as the paste goes in, so that the sauce tastes raw and tinny.
mistakes.fix: Fry the paste in the fat first until it darkens.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving it too long over high heat, so that it turns black and bitter.
mistakes.fix: Stir all the time and add the liquid as soon as it sticks.

quiz.question: Why fry tomato paste before adding liquid?
choices: To make it raw-tasting and sharp.
To turn its tinny taste sweet and rich.
quiz.because: Frying in fat changes the taste of the paste.

quiz.question: What do you do while the paste fries?
choices: Leave it alone until it smokes.
quiz.because: Stirring keeps it from burning as it darkens.

quiz.question: What colour tells you it is ready?
quiz.because: Brick red means it has cooked without burning.

quiz.question: The sauce tastes tinny and sharp. What would you change next time?
choices: Fry the paste longer in the fat before adding liquid.
quiz.because: A tinny taste means the paste was not cooked long enough.
